extracted.intended_audience: teachers, educators, students of pedagogy, and readers interested in reflective thinking and instructional method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for fostering and evaluating reflective thinking in learners and for structuring instruction so principles, application, imagination, and habit are balanced. Includes criteria for when to make assumptions explicit, how to use play and work, and how to present familiar and remote material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality should be tested by application
rubrics_metrics.description: "The essence of the general is application." A genuine generalization is one that extends itself spontaneously to new cases; spurious generalizations fail this test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test general statements by attempting application; watch for principles that are verbally general but lack discernment of meaning. The failure of a principle to extend itself signals it is spurious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises must give insight, not merely drill
rubrics_metrics.description: The true purpose of exercises that apply rules and principles is not so much to drive or drill them in as to give adequate insight into an idea or principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating application as a separate final step. Exercises should enlarge and test meaning by using it in judgment; artificial tasks invented solely to secure application are misguided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles must be flexible, not fossilized
rubrics_metrics.description: When the general meaning is regarded as complete in itself, application is treated as an external use and principles become fossilized and rigid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor moving ideas that seek outlet and application. A 'true conception' is a moving idea that naturally applies to particulars; avoid presenting principles as isolated, immutable formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide conditions favorable to natural application
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher needs to supply conditions favorable to use and exercise; but something is wrong when artificial tasks have arbitrarily to be invented in order to secure application for principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning situations so that application emerges organically from problems and context rather than forcing contrived exercises whose only aim is to practice a named principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make implicit assumptions explicit when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If two persons find themselves at cross-purposes, it is necessary to dig up and compare the presuppositions... The implicit is made explicit; what was unconsciously assumed is exposed to the light of conscious day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When misunderstandings or conflicts arise, identify and articulate the background assumptions. Conscious inspection of unconscious presuppositions removes roots of misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nurture the tact to balance unconscious and conscious
rubrics_metrics.description: No rules can be laid down for attaining the due balance and rhythm of these two phases of mental life... our reliance must be upon the disposition and tact of the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should develop judgment and disposition that allow individuals to know how far to make assumptions explicit; there is no one-size-fits-all rule—assessments should value this cultivated balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-analytic instruction that pries into the familiar
rubrics_metrics.description: To pry into the familiar, the usual, the automatic, simply for the sake of making it conscious, simply for the sake of formulating it, is both an impertinent interference, and a source of boredom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force learners to formulate every habitual step; over-analytic methods that compel conscious attention to smoothly-working attitudes produce ennui and reduce interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conscious formulation to detect error and clinch truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The detection of error, the clinching of truth, demand conscious statement... Where the shoe pinches, analytic examination is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage explicit review and summarizing when needed to solidify knowledge and prevent errors from being repeated. In later stages of learning, conscious condensation and review are imperative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate projection (going ahead) and reflection (turning back)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projection and reflection, going directly ahead and turning back in scrutiny, should alternate. Unconsciousness gives spontaneity and freshness; consciousness, conviction and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional design and evaluation should look for cycles of exploration and reflective consolidation rather than continuous one-mode activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance process and product (play and work)
rubrics_metrics.description: In play, interest centers in activity; in work, the end holds attention. The contrast is one of emphasis, not of cleavage; isolation of one from the other is harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster both engagement in activity (process) and orientation toward worthwhile ends (product). Avoid isolating play from purpose or making every task solely outcome-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent 'fooling' by linking play to results
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fooling" is a series of disconnected temporary overflows of energy dependent upon whim and accident... The only way of preventing this consequence is to make regard for results enter into even the freest play activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow free play but ensure it has some relation to outcomes or purposes so it does not become aimless; design playful tasks that still connect to learning goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent drudgery by transferring interest from ends to means
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive interest in the result alters work to drudgery... Willingness to work for ends by means of acts not naturally attractive is best attained by securing such an appreciation of the value of the end that a sense of its value is transferred to its means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tasks are uninteresting, cultivate appreciation of the end so learners derive interest in the means; avoid imposing repulsive tasks as mere discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate the unity of playfulness and seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: To be playful and serious at the same time is possible, and it defines the ideal mental condition... Mental play is open-mindedness, faith in the power of thought to preserve its own integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value openness, curiosity, and accurate noting of results together. Assessors should look for both imaginative exploration and earnest, accurate recording and use of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher as artist: harmonize idea and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher's claim to rank as an artist is measured by his ability to foster the attitude of the artist... To nurture inspiring aim and executive means into harmony with each other is at once the difficulty and the reward of the teacher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should both inspire large ideas and develop skillful execution. Evaluation of teaching should consider whether skill-training is accompanied by enlargement of mental vision and power of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance the far (novel) and the near (familiar)
rubrics_metrics.description: The more remote supplies the stimulus and the motive; the nearer at hand furnishes the point of approach and the available resources... The best thinking occurs when the easy and the difficult are duly proportioned to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present material so that novel elements stimulate inquiry while familiar elements provide handles for understanding; avoid only presenting the familiar (which won't excite thought) or only the remote (which lacks a basis for comprehension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present the familiar under unusual conditions to stimulate thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: The familiar and the near do not excite or repay thought on their own account, but only as they are adjusted to mastering the strange and remote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get learners to think about familiar things, reframe them in novel contexts or pose problems that make the familiar serve as a resource for solving unfamiliar problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use imagination to supplement observation, not replace it
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination supplements and deepens observation; only when it turns into the fanciful does it become a substitute for observation and lose logical force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage imaginative realization of remote or absent realities (history, principles, geometry) while maintaining connection to observable facts; avoid presenting facts as hard, ready-made articles that leave no room for imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate to enrich personal experience, not to swamp it
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction always runs the risk of swamping the pupil's own vital, though narrow, experience under masses of communicated material... The instructor ceases and the teacher begins at the point where communicated matter stimulates into fuller and more significant life that which has entered by the strait and narrow gate of sense-perception and motor activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communication so it stimulates and enlarges learners' own experience rather than replacing it. Genuine communication should produce a community of thought and purpose between learner and cultural material.
